dissents.topic: Severity of the setuptools<82 cap leaking into core/setup.py runtime install_requires

positions.position: P1 — build-time constraint leaked into runtime install_requires; documentation/literate hygiene concern, suggests moving to CI/build constraints file
P1 — complects build-time CI workaround with runtime dependency contract; should not have shipped at all (the 'one line that should not have shipped')
P1 — exports a CI workaround as a permanent constraint on every downstream user; pull it out unless runtime-justified, otherwise NEEDS-WORK
P1 — LEAKY-ABSTRACTION; boundary violation between build-system and runtime contract
P1 — wrong data shape; CI scripts own CI pins, package metadata owns runtime needs; strip it out
P1 — frame widened beyond bug; REFUSED until either justified as runtime requirement or moved to CI layer

dissents.topic: Severity of the unexplained mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 bump

positions.position: P2 — separate change folded into same commit with no stated reason
P2 — separate risk surface complected into the same commit; bisection becomes harder
P2 — part of 'THREE-PATCHES masquerading as one'; not obviously required by the mmengine/setuptools issue
P2 — undocumented contract change; needs one-line comment on why 3.3.0 was chosen
P2 — behavior change folded into a CI-fix PR with no mention; needs a one-line note
P2 — either justified or dropped; bundled changes erode ability to reason about future failures
P1 — silently changes the build contract; introduces an ordering invariant (setuptools<82 must precede mmcv install) that must be stated
P2 — place-oriented coupling to global mutable state; less reproducible
P2 — real behavioral change; deserves one sentence in the commit message explaining why mim was abandoned
P2 — fragile and underexplained; FIXME doesn't capture the local ordering constraint
P1 — TESTED-NOT-PROVED; no stated invariant for the CI environment under which the source build terminates successfully

issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaked into core/setup.py runtime install_requires instead of CI/build-only constraint
issues.detail: The cap belongs to the build environment (mmcv/mmengine still call pkg_resources, which setuptools 82 removed). Putting setuptools<82 into core/setup.py extras_require/install_requires propagates this constraint to every downstream consumer of autogluon.core forever — not just CI. setuptools is a build-time tool, not a runtime dep, and this exports a transient CI workaround as a permanent constraint on every user's environment for a problem they will never encounter. Either justify it as a runtime requirement or move it to the CI/build layer where it actually belongs.

issues.description: core/setup.py setuptools<82 pin has no FIXME/comment tying it to the upstream cause
issues.detail: Two of the three pin sites (env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh) carry FIXME comments pointing at mmcv issue 3325; core/setup.py has no such breadcrumb. When upstream resolves the issue, a future maintainer must do archaeology across three files to find and remove this cap, and the published-package site has the weakest signal. A single named marker (e.g. MMCV_3325_WORKAROUND) at every site with the precise removal condition would make cleanup mechanical instead of forgotten.

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation silently changes the build contract and adds an undocumented ordering invariant
issues.detail: Switching from `mim install mmcv==2.1.0` to `pip install mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation` means mmcv is now built against whatever setuptools/torch/numpy happen to be in the ambient environment, instead of an isolated build env constructed from pyproject.toml. This introduces a load-bearing ordering constraint (setuptools<82 must already be installed before mmcv is built) that is nowhere stated. It also abandons mim's selection of prebuilt wheels matching torch/cuda, forcing a source build that depends on whatever compiler/torch/CUDA happen to be present. No invariant is stated under which this command is known to terminate.

issues.description: FIXME comments lack a stated termination/removal condition
issues.detail: The patch labels the constraint with FIXME and a link to an upstream issue, but states no falsifiable condition for removal — no precise upstream tag/version, no precondition stating exactly which mmcv/mmengine versions require pkg_resources, no postcondition stating when the cap may be lifted. A FIXME without a termination function is a smuggled goto into the future of the build system; it will not be reasoned about, only forgotten. Compounded by the fact that env_setup.sh says 'remove cap once fixed' while setup_mmcv.sh says 'revert mmcv installation to use mim once fixed' — the workaround spans multiple sites with partial revert instructions.

issues.description: Three changes bundled into one PR/commit (setuptools cap, mmengine source swap, mmdet version bump)
issues.detail: The diff conflates three independent changes: (1) cap setuptools<82 to dodge the mmcv build break, (2) replace pinned mmengine git SHA with PyPI wheel 0.10.7, (3) bump mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0. Each can fail independently and deserves its own bisect target. The PR title is 'Fix mmengine failure' which only covers part of the diff. If a regression appears, bisection cannot separate the mmdet bump from the setuptools cap from the mmengine source change.

issues.description: mmdet bumped 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 with no stated rationale
issues.detail: The PR framing is about mmengine/setuptools but silently bumps mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0. Either it is forced by the new mmengine 0.10.7 pin (in which case state it) or it is unrelated drift (in which case it should be its own change). A reviewer auditing this PR cannot tell which from the diff alone, and there is no subtype/contract verification that mmdet 3.3.0 preserves the postconditions that downstream multimodal code depends on.

issues.description: Same setuptools<82 cap duplicated across three sites with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The pin lives in env_setup.sh (build_pkg), setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py. When mmcv#3325 is fixed, someone must remember all three sites and unwind them in sync. If the cap is lifted in one place and not the others, the workaround partially persists in ways that are hard to detect. A single shared variable, env var, or single FIXME-tracked location would make the cleanup obvious.

issues.description: Removed pinned mmengine git SHA without recording whether 0.10.7 still contains the torch 2.5 fix
issues.detail: The previous code installed mmengine from a specific git SHA chosen 'with the fix for torch 2.5.' The new code installs mmengine==0.10.7 from PyPI, but the comment explaining why a specific mmengine version was required is gone. If 0.10.7 predates or lacks the torch 2.5 fix the previous SHA was chosen for, the torch 2.5 compatibility postcondition is now weaker than before — an LSP-style regression at the dependency-graph level. The fact that mattered ('we need a torch-2.5-compatible mmengine') is no longer represented anywhere.

issues.description: PR description is empty for a CI-unblocking change that pins a major build tool
issues.detail: The PR body contains no statement of the problem, the reasoning, or the chosen resolution. The reader is forced to reverse-engineer the fix from the diff and an external issue link. For a workaround that pins setuptools, switches mmcv install method, and bumps mmdet, the body should state: which CI job broke, the error signature, the upstream issue link, the precondition (setuptools 82 removed pkg_resources), the postcondition (CI green with the listed versions), the rationale for the mim->pip switch, and the termination condition for the FIXME.

issues.description: Ordering of pip install commands is load-bearing but undocumented
issues.detail: The script now installs setuptools<82, then mmcv with --no-build-isolation, then mmengine, then mmdet. Correctness depends on mmcv being built before later installs trigger setuptools upgrades, and on pip's resolver not upgrading setuptools mid-sequence. A one-line comment stating the invariant 'setuptools<82 must hold throughout all four installs' would convert folklore into explicit reasoning and prevent a future maintainer from 'cleaning up' the pip install setuptools<82 line and silently breaking the build.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converge unanimously on the panel's strongest claim: the setuptools<82 cap added to core/setup.py is a build-time CI workaround that has leaked into the published package's runtime dependency contract, and it should be either justified as a true runtime requirement or moved back to the CI/build layer (Hickey: 'the one line that should not have shipped'; Dijkstra: REFUSED until corrected; Torvalds/Pike: strip it out). Secondary concerns echoed by most reviewers: this is three changes bundled in one PR (setuptools cap, mmengine source swap from git SHA to PyPI wheel, mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 bump) with an empty PR body and an unexplained mmdet version bump, plus the switch to --no-build-isolation introduces an undocumented ordering invariant on the install sequence. The FIXME comments rightly point at upstream mmcv#3325 but lack a termination/removal condition and are duplicated across three sites with no single source of truth. The largest preserved disagreement is on framing severity for --no-build-isolation: Knuth and Dijkstra treat it as P1 (changes the build contract / TESTED-NOT-PROVED with no stated invariant) while Hickey, Torvalds, and Pike treat it as P2 (real coupling but tolerable with a comment). The CI fix itself will likely make today's build green; what is missing is the explanation, scoping, and termination criteria a future maintainer needs to safely unwind it.
